label: prose:sm-params-higgs
title: Higgs sector (2)
html:
Parameter Framework status Anchor
m_H conjectural — T(2,8) torus-link identification; ratio-level numerics within a factor of two electroweak triplet
v (electroweak scale) open —

The Higgs mass has a conjectural identification: the Higgs is assigned the torus link T(2,8) within the electroweak triplet conjecture, alongside W = T(2,4) and Z = T(2,6). Because torus links have zero hyperbolic volume, the mass chain for these carriers is not the volume–density chain but a Reshetikhin–Turaev evaluation at a root of unity, and that chain has two open inputs: the level selection and the invariant-to-mass formula. The best numerical probes land within a factor of two of m_H; a factor of two is not a prediction, and no formula currently gives unity.

The electroweak scale v has no derivation. The vacuum-vortex morphism proposed in the G-action-on-substrate conjecture is the natural home for it, but that conjecture is itself open at the closure level, and no computation extracts v (equivalently the Fermi constant) from the substrate. Since v normalises every Standard-Model mass via the Yukawa mechanism, its absence means the framework's mass predictions proceed by an entirely different route (calibrated volume–density and Hecke-energy chains) — a structural divergence from the Standard Model parameterisation that any completed derivation would need to reconcile.
